title: half-life 2: update
text: This is the Half Life 2 version of a wine-tasting party. People are going to stand around talking intensely about how they can really notice the woodsy undertones mixed with a slight chocolate after-taste. You're going to sit there sipping wine... and all you taste is wine ... and then another wine ... and another ... and they all taste the same. But, wait.. this one is slightly sweeter then that one, so that's something. And then the wine snobs look at you, roll their eyes after you make that observation, and whisper to their friends that they can't believe you can't tell the differences. Another example is when my girlfriend's paternal twin nephews come over. I can't tell the apart, but she says "that one has XYZ that is different, it's so easy to tell them apart." It's easy if you've spent a lot of time with them. Not so easy if you haven't. Essentially that is what this mod makes you feel like ... a clueless idiot that's staring at things intently trying to detect changes. Instead of going "omg, look what they did there! Holy cow, fantastic!" you're going to be going "This looks exactly the same except... is the texture different? No, there's a shader applied to this now? I ...♥♥♥♥♥♥I can't tell." The things that stood out for me were translucency. The options menu is now slightly translucent. Breen's intro display is slightly transparent ... certain things do stick out. But, they leave you with a "oh... ok, I see what they did there, but ... uh, what about the rest?" I played this using a GTX760 with all settings maxed, bloom turned on, etc, etc. Unless there's some magical .ini files I need to tweak without realizing it, I just don't see enough visual change and impact from this mod to warrant installing it. I know they put a lot of time into it, but spending years polishing a piece of silver to get a tiny bit more shine on it is going to be lost on the lay person. I sound like a complete **** ripping on them like this, but I actually totally understand. I'm in love with the game FUEL to the extent that I went into its HLSL shader files, did a huge overhaul, added in extra effects and polished others. I've spent months fiddling around with things to get them "just right". End result? You can barely notice any changes I've made. So, I never bothered uploading it to the community. It's "death of a thousand cuts" and while the modders know every single one of the 1000 cuts they made, the lay person only notices like 5 or 6 which means the work spent on the other 900+ is in essence wasted effort to the lay man. But, hey, if it makes you feel better doing it, then more power to you. (That's why I did the FUEL shaders... I liked tweaking the code, even if the end result was minimal at best.) I think the main reason it's so hard to tell any difference is: a) the world vertices/polygons are still just as blocky as they were back then, but they did this to keep the original look/feel (IE: no higher-polygon models, no added poly's to environment to smooth out corners and such) b) the textures look the exact same... I didn't notice any new whiz-bang things like bump-mapping or such to make the environment look more real instead of a flat hollywood movie set. Maybe a texture or two was a tad sharper? I just don't know ... and that's what's irking me. I don't know really what changed, I don't know what I'm missing, I don't know where to look to go "ah, yeah, see what you did there ... good job, mate!" This mod makes me feel like I'm standing next to someone that sees something special, is trying to point it out to me, and it's flying right over my head making me feel like a clueless idiot. But I digress... On the plus-side, the commentary part is really, really good. The player insights are actually really entertaining, and often easy to empathize with (since you may have had a similar experience or feeling playing the game). As a technical accomplishment, though, since that's what it's primary purpose is, I just have to unfortunately give this a thumbs down. The Cinematic Mode mod provides a far more stark contrast between old and new HL2. (Except that mod goes nuts with character model overhauls that tend to irk purists). Again, I feel really bad ripping on them like this, but I just don't see any amazing impact this mod does to warrant installing it other then the additional commentary mode.

title: half-life: blue shift
text: Having played "Half-Life" and "Half-Life: Opposing Force," I was ready to complete the set and play "Half-Life: Blue Force." When I played it, It felt a bit lacking, but it still managed to have charm. It still maintains what made the other two games work, in terms of it's story and it's engagement. You play as one of the "red shirts" (or as in this case, blue shirts), aka, a Security Guard, Barney Calhoun. He's one of the lowly security guards in the Black Mesa compound who, surprisingly, proves more badass than most of his own coworkers. Again, for the same reason I enjoyed playing as Gordon Freeman in HL and as Adrian Shepherd in HL:OF, Barney is a character that can get very immersive, owing to his silence. And you never lose control of him in the game, keeping you firmly in his POV. Most of what I have to say about this game has already been said in my other reviews of HL and HL:OF, so I won't go into too much detail. I liked the continuous level design, giving the feel of exploration, and enough of a story that will keep you invested in the game. I also liked how this game used armor instead of a powered suit, making it easier to maintain by just findining more armor, preventing you from slowing down too much. But therein lies the problem. Whereas "Opposing Force" had plenty of new stuff, this game feels lacking. You only get a few of the weapons from the first game, and this game is much shorter compared to the first game. I feel this game fell short of it's predecessor by not trying anything new to expand upon the story and setting. I am glad though that there isn't as much platforming as the original, like in HL:OF, which did the same. But the one thing that saved it for me was how they made you feel more involved in the plot, near the climax of the game. But overall, I feel this game could have been so much more. While this expansion didn't have what "Opposing Force" has to offer, it still manages to work fine on it's own, and it's not terrible. It's enough to keep you invested, but it's kind of a letdown after a good game and a good expansion pack. But if I had to play it again, I'd play it again, soundly.
